question: Can a small learned Korean text model distinguish explicit reporting errors from substantive changes and ground previous/current monetary values in text spans across unseen wording families?
scope: Short, selected Korean monetary-policy passages; not document retrieval, legal interpretation, multi-document entity resolution, or complete fact checking.

label_definition.correction: An asserted correction of an explicitly erroneous earlier monetary report.
label_definition.policy_change: An asserted substantive monetary change, not correction of an erroneous report.
label_definition.equivalent: An explicitly stated restatement of the same amount in different units.
label_definition.undetermined: The passage does not assert one of those relations: missing reason, denied change/correction, conditional scenario, proposal, or incomparable items. This is a semantic class, distinct from model abstention.

authorship: Independent personal follow-up directed by soccz; code, synthetic examples and provisional labels created with AI assistance. No independent human annotation.
development_context: All v1 results and examples have already been inspected. V1 is regression/development evidence, never a new blind test. V2 grammar is designed by the same author as the method; held-out surface families are not independent human or population validation.

data.per_frame_family: All four relation classes; previous/current textual order balanced, independent distractor monetary span; undetermined subtypes rotate.
data.split: Distinct fictional names, years and value ranges; no exact passage overlap. Every frame is rendered in every family in its split. Semantic frame is the bootstrap unit.

method.relation: Character TF-IDF 2-5 grams, sublinear TF, min_df=2; logistic regression C=10, max_iter=1000. All numeric/currency spans masked before vectorization.
method.arguments: The same classifier recipe predicts previous/current/other for each regex-extracted monetary span from 48 characters of left/right context, with all other numbers masked. No gold construction metadata is passed to prediction. Role training uses determinate examples only; relation=undetermined suppresses arguments.
method.constraints: For a determinate relation require exactly one previous and one current span, equal normalized amounts for equivalent, unequal amounts for correction/change. Unsupported parses or failures abstain. An undetermined prediction returns no monetary relation.
method.selection: On validation only, choose maximum-coverage threshold among 0, .05, ..., .95, .99 with at least 20 accepted items and joint error <=5%; ties choose smaller threshold. If no candidate qualifies, abstain on every item. No guarantee on evaluation risk.
method.gpu: None; deterministic CPU linear classifiers, not another neural-model fine-tuning run.

comparisons: learned relation with local span arguments
metrics: joint relation and argument exact match
coverage and joint error among answered items
statistics: 10000 paired bootstrap resamples of the 48 semantic frames, seed 731; conditions fixed. Intervals conditional on authored templates and frames; not independent annotation/template/population uncertainty.
stopping: Freeze input/method/evaluation code before model fitting; run once, retain failures, independently recalculate metrics and validate spans, publish measured results and limits. Do not tune to evaluation scores.
disclosure: No customer data or delivery implementation. Synthetic data and independent implementation may be published. Official excerpts, if used, are short attributed case studies with provisional labels; raw fetched pages stay local.
